metaTitle: Running Toilet Repair in Burbank, CA | $135–$220
metaDescription: Toilet won't stop running? Get it fixed in Burbank for $135–$220. Common in post-war homes with original plumbing parts.
intro: A toilet that keeps running after you flush is one of the most common plumbing complaints in Burbank, especially in the post-war single-family homes that make up much of the city's housing stock. Many of these houses still have original plumbing components or fixtures that have never been replaced, so worn-out internal parts are often the culprit. Left alone, a running toilet can waste a surprising amount of water and add up on your bill.
causes: A worn or misaligned flapper valve that no longer seals the tank properly.
A fill valve that has degraded over time, which is common in older Burbank homes with original toilet hardware.
The float is set too high, causing water to constantly drain into the overflow tube.
Mineral buildup or sediment in the tank, which is more common in homes with older galvanized supply lines.
A cracked or corroded overflow tube that lets water leak out continuously.
whatProDoes: Inspects the tank to identify whether the flapper, fill valve, float, or overflow tube is causing the issue.
Shuts off the water supply and drains the tank to safely access the internal components.
Replaces or adjusts the faulty part, such as swapping a worn flapper or installing a new fill valve.
Tests the flush and refill cycle several times to confirm the toilet shuts off correctly.
Checks for related issues, like slow leaks or corrosion, that are more common in homes with original plumbing.
Cleans up the work area and leaves the tank lid properly seated.
diyOrPro: If you're comfortable removing the tank lid and can identify a simple, inexpensive part like the flapper, replacing it yourself is generally low-risk since it doesn't involve gas lines or water heaters. However, if the problem persists after a flapper swap, or if you notice corrosion, a cracked tank, or issues with the shutoff valve itself, it's worth calling a pro rather than risking a bigger leak or water damage, particularly in older homes where original valves can be brittle or hard to shut off completely.
priceNote: This job runs $135 to $220 in Burbank, based on a $94/hour rate and a typical job length of 1 to 2 hours. The final cost within that range depends on which part needs replacing and whether the shutoff valve or supply line shows wear common in homes with original plumbing.

faqs.q: Why won't my toilet stop running even after I jiggle the handle?
faqs.a: Jiggling the handle sometimes repositions a worn flapper temporarily, but if it keeps running, the flapper likely needs replacing, or the issue could be the fill valve or float instead.

faqs.q: Is a running toilet actually costing me money?
faqs.a: Yes, a continuously running toilet can waste a significant amount of water over time, which shows up as a higher water bill even if the leak seems minor.

faqs.q: Will the plumber need to replace the whole toilet?
faqs.a: Usually not. Most running toilet issues are fixed by replacing an internal part like the flapper, fill valve, or float, not the entire fixture.
